title: JAS (Boko Haram Faction) Massacres 57 Civilians in Kukawa, Borno State
detail: Jama'atu Ahlis Sunna Lidda'awati wal-Jihad (JAS), the original Boko Haram faction, attacked the villages of Mallam Karamti and Kwatandashi in Kukawa Local Government Area near Baga town, Borno State, accusing residents of spying for the rival ISWAP faction. An estimated 100 civilians were seized from their homes; 57 bodies were later recovered and approximately 70 people remained missing. The massacre is one of the deadliest single JAS attacks in 2026 and reflects intensifying violence between JAS and ISWAP for territorial control in the Lake Chad Basin — an intra-jihadist rivalry that increasingly victimizes civilian populations caught between the two factions.

title: Mass School Abductions in Borno and Oyo: 88+ Seized in Single Day
detail: In dual mass abductions on May 15, armed groups seized students and teachers across two states simultaneously. In Askira-Uba LGA, Borno State, Boko Haram gunmen invaded the Primary and Junior Government Day Secondary School in Mussa-Biri community, abducting an estimated 42–82 students and teachers according to various tallies (Senator Mohammed Ali Ndume confirmed 42; Amnesty International cited up to 82). Separately, in Oriire LGA, Oyo State, bandits simultaneously attacked three schools — Baptist Nursery and Primary School (Yawota), Community High School (Ahoro-Esinele), and L.A. Primary School (Esiele) — seizing 46 persons (7 teachers and 39 students), killing an assistant headmaster and an okada rider, and wounding two Amotekun Corps operatives. Amnesty International stated at least 82 schoolchildren were abducted across the two states between May 13–15, calling it a wave of terror against Nigeria's education sector.
